definition: a small tree-dwelling rodent with a long bushy tail
hook: The Greeks named the squirrel after what it does with its tail.
modernAnchor: A flick of grey up a tree trunk, a tail like a question mark. We call it a squirrel.
journey: Greek skia meant shadow and oura meant tail. Put together, skiouros, the shadow-tailed one.
Ancient writers said the animal sat upright and held that tail over itself like a parasol, shading its own body.
Latin took it as sciurus, Old French wore it down to esquirel, and English borrowed that in the 1300s.
Every sound has shifted since, but the picture underneath has not moved: an animal sitting in the shade it carries.
